steps.name: DESeq2 Wald test HFD vs chow with apeglm shrinkage
caveats: A quantifier name alone does not establish that the length correction occurred. If the counts come from Salmon, kallisto, or RSEM as a gene-level table, with no per-sample quantification files and no average transcript length table, the import state is not established. Ask for the per-sample quantification files, quant.sf, abundance.h5, or genes.results, or for the average transcript length table per gene and sample. If neither arrives, fit the count model on the counts as delivered, with no length offset, and state in the plan and in the report that the length offset is lost and that a change in isoform use can show as differential expression. Do not run tximport on a gene table, because tximport imports transcript estimates, and do not invent a length input.
In a cell with fewer than seven replicates DESeq2 flags a count outlier by Cook's distance and sets p-value and padj to NA; report the count of such genes apart from independent-filtering NAs.
The size factor of the low-depth sample sample_01 scales its expected counts, so depth alone does not bias the fold change; the model correctly gives it a wider interval.

plan.title: HFD vs chow liver DE and hallmark GSEA
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is 12000 mouse gene-symbol counts from Salmon for 12 liver samples (6 high-fat diet vs 6 chow, unpaired, single batch), with sample_01 at ~4x below the median library size. The plan follows the sourced two-group count procedure: (1) blind-VST sample-structure QC that keeps and inspects the shallow sample rather than silently dropping it; (2) a DESeq2 Wald test on the counts as delivered — no length offset is applied because the Salmon-derived gene table carries no per-sample quantification or average-transcript-length input, and tximport cannot be run on a gene table — with a minimal pre-filter, median-of-ratios size factors (which absorb the depth difference of sample_01 as wider intervals, not bias), apeglm shrinkage, and BH at alpha 0.05 with independent filtering; (3) a preranked fgsea GSEA of the full Wald-statistic-ranked list against the staged MSigDB mouse Hallmark collection (MGI symbols, 2026.1), which shares the gene-symbol identifier space of the counts; and (4) a report that gives both unshrunken and shrunken fold changes, fit diagnostics, p-value histogram, leading-edge genes per significant set, and the full reproducibility record. No cell-type, survival, or translational steps are included because the question asks only which genes and hallmark pathways change.

fgsea preranked GSEA on the Wald statistic with MSigDB mouse Hallmark
